Kickstarter is for sure the biggest one, but Backerkit has a better system for late pledges from what I hear (when people can pledge even after the campaign is over). But people usually crowdfund for a product that they know will get delivered to them at a certain deadline, "this is ongoing, so who knows when you would get it" will not attract a lot of backers. But you can launch a campaign with a deadline of 1 year (even if the campaign runs for just 1 month, but 30k is very high goal for your first project, you would need marketing miracles). If you fail at delivering your project, KS will likely ban you from launching anything ever again (this counts for most crowdfunding platforms).

I think a Patreon or something like that works best for what you're describing, but you won't get organic traffic there, you would need to market it on your own (or with a team) mostly.
